text: The Execute Pipeline activity lets a pipeline invoke a completely different pipeline as one of its own activities. Select an existing pipeline, then supply values for whatever parameters that pipeline actually expects — the exact same parameter mechanism from Lesson 17, just passed pipeline to pipeline instead of run to run.

Notice the parameter value here: item dot SourceTable. This is exactly how a ForEach and an Execute Pipeline combine in practice, passing each iteration's current item straight into the inner pipeline as a genuine parameter, not a shared variable.

This one activity genuinely solves three real problems. It works around ForEach's no-nesting limit, since a ForEach can contain an Execute Pipeline whose target has its own inner loop. It groups several activities that would otherwise clutter a single loop iteration into one clean call. And it enables real reuse — one well-built pipeline, called from several different parents, each with different parameter values.

waitOnCompletion true, the default, makes the outer pipeline wait for the inner one to finish, with its status and any error flowing straight back up. Set it to false instead, and the outer pipeline fires the inner one and moves on immediately — useful for genuinely independent work, though the outer pipeline won't actually know whether the inner one succeeded.
